reason: Conversation 1 adapts to the customer's constraint that the unit can't be unplugged, asks relevant questions (beep or warning, restart behaviour, release button feel), advises cleaning the latch area, and ends with a clear recommendation to book a Bosch engineer. It is a little overconfident in naming the door interlock microswitch, though it doesn't push the customer to buy a part. Conversation 2 repeatedly suggests unplugging after being told that's impossible, and it gives an incorrect instruction to look at the door 'with it unplugged'. It also asks the customer to 'plug it back in and try a cup of water', and its final escalation is terse and ends with an odd leftover 'Next:' prompt. It does pick up on the useful detail that the fault happens more when the door is closed gently, and it eventually recommends an engineer, but the process is much less coherent.
